correctness.rationale: The generating function is algebraically factored and yields strictly positive summable compound-Poisson coefficients. For all j>=1, a two-case exact inequality bounds r^j(1-r) by q^j(1-q)+q^{2j}(1-q^2), using the maximizer j/(j+1) and explicit >1/2 endpoint bounds; this proves strict canonical monotonicity, not finite enumeration. The standard discrete canonical-sequence theorem then proves binomial-thinning self-decomposability. Exact rational calculations independently verify formulas and the generic-mixture contrast.

originality.rationale: The full 2023 PoiTG preprint gives the convolution and PGF, and the 2016 parent paper explicitly proves ordinary infinite divisibility (which is not claimed as new here). Neither gives the exact all-index decreasing canonical sequence for the PoiTG family or a binomial-thinning decomposition. Pakes (2022) supplies the general criterion, not this coupled-rate inequality; a counterexample eliminates any generic two-geometric-mixture implication. Relevant prior claims and literature were compared; an unindexed stronger source remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The theorem establishes a complete all-parameter structural property for a published count distribution: it gives exact compound-Poisson rates, justifies existence of stationary binomial-thinning autoregressive representations, and implies unimodality. The proof uses a nontrivial all-index inequality; an explicit nonselfdecomposable two-geometric mixture shows this is not a routine generic mixture closure.
